 Show Most recent Most popular 'They have paid a lot of respect to the competition and us' published at 19:29 GMT 19:29 GMT 
 Fleetwood Town v Arsenal (20:00 GMT) 
 Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor, speaking to Sky Sports on his team selection: "We made two changes, one enforced through suspension. We had to make changes because we have a packed schedule and we have the champions coming to town and there's a way we want to go and play."
 On what challenge Arsenal present: "The steepest from winning the league last year. It will be a very difficult challenge we have to come up against. They have paid a lot of respect to the competition and us by naming such a strong team. We understand it's a difficult challenge."
 9 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Fleetwood on best League Cup run published at 19:27 GMT 19:27 GMT 
 Fleetwood Town v Arsenal (20:00 GMT) 
 League Two Fleetwood have finished 15th and 14th since being relegated in 2024.
 But they're currently on their best-ever run in the Carabao Cup, so, for tonight at least, things are looking rosy. 
 Can they cause an almighty upset and book their spot in the quarter-finals?
 Image source, Getty Images 
 4 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Fleetwood team will see it as a real opportunity to make history' published at 19:24 GMT 19:24 GMT 
 Fleetwood Town v Arsenal (20:00 GMT) 
 Leon Osman 
Former Everton midfielder on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 As neutral fans we always get excited about the possibility of seeing a giant killer in these situations, and with the mentality of this Fleetwood team, they will see it as a real opportunity to make history. 
 To put down one of those results that will always be remembered.
 18 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Arsenal looking for first League Cup win since 1993 published at 19:22 GMT 19:22 GMT 
 Fleetwood v Arsenal (20:00 GMT) 
 The thing about Arsenal is that they've only won the League Cup twice, and never since 1993. 
 They were beaten in the final last year by Manchester City, will they finally get number three this season?
 Image source, Getty Images 
 45 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:21 GMT 19:21 GMT 
 Speaking of Arsenal. They're also playing tonight...

 Post published at 19:20 GMT 19:20 GMT 
 Bradford v Peterborough (19:45 GMT) 
 Bradford are making their first fourth-round appearance in this competition since their magical run to the final in 2012-13.
 They beat Arsenal on penalties that year.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 19 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:18 GMT 19:18 GMT 
 Bradford v Peterborough (19:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Peterborough also have a relatively new manager in the hot seat.
 Robbie Savage, heard of him? The former Birmingham midfielder, Match of the Day pundit and Macclesfield boss took over a Posh side who had collected just one point from their opening seven league games.
 Savage has started to turn things around with a first-match win over Leicester, but two points from their last three games mean Peterborough aren't out of the bottom four, yet.
 A first win at Valley Parade in nine years tonight though could be the confidence boost Posh needs.
 15 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:16 GMT 19:16 GMT 
 Bradford v Peterborough (19:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Bradford may be in the fourth round, but their manager Michael Duff is leading them in this competition for the very first time.
 Their previous cup wins, against Rochdale, Burnley and Leyton Orient, all came under Graham Alexander who took over at Preston last month.
 Bradford haven't conceded a goal yet under their new manager and are currently on an 11-match unbeaten run!
 15 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 19:14 GMT 19:14 GMT 
 Bradford v Peterborough (19:45 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images At least one League One club will be in the quarters with Bradford City hosting Peterbourough United in tonight's earlier game.
 The Bantams are flying high in the third tier, up in third, and haven't lost since September 1st (2-1 against Cambridge, thanks for asking). 
 Peterborough meanwhile are in the bottom three with just two league wins all season.
 The Posh really are up against it tonight. The two clubs met earlier in the season too, in the league on the opening day, with Bradford winning 2-0.

 Team news - four changes for both sides published at 19:06 GMT 19:06 GMT 
 Bradford v Peterborough (19:45 GMT) 
 Michael Duff makes four changes to his Bradford City side that drew 0-0 with Oxford United in League One at the weekend.
 Reece Welch, Macaulay Gillesphey, Jake Beesley and Bobby Pointon all come into the starting XI.
 Bradford XI: McCracken, Pennington, Welch, Gillesphey, O'Keeffe, Sarcevic, Connolly, Touray, Lapslie, Pointon, Beesley
 Subs: Baldwin, Cartwright, Dawson, Jackson, Matthews, Morgan, Phillips, Pratt, Swan
 It's four changes for the Peterborough XI too after the 1-1 draw at Bromley in League One.
 Josh Feeney, Brandon Khela, Vernon Masara and Danny Ormerod are given the nod by Robbie Savage.
 Peterborough XI: Bass, Johnston, Feeney, Mills, Ashfield, Khela, Edwards, Williams, Masara, Ormerod
 Subs: Andeng-Ndi, Dornelly, Frith, Garbett, Jones, Kelly, Shofowoke, Sykut, Weir
 6 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team news - Meslier and O'Neill make debuts, Dowman starts published at 19:04 GMT 19:04 GMT 
 Fleetwood Town v Arsenal (20:00 GMT) 
 Matt Lawlor makes two changes to his Fleetwood side that fell to a 2-1 defeat at Exeter City in League Two at the weekend.
 Rhys Bennett and Aaron Loupalo-Bi come in for Lewis McCann and Ronan Coughlan.
 Andy Cannon returns from injury to make the bench, while Finley Potter starts despite suffering a nasty cut above his eye against Exeter.
 Fleetwood XI: Lynch, Rooney, Bennett, Potter, Haughey, McLean, Neal, Helm, Batty, Evans, Loupalo-Bi. 
 Subs : Pradic, Andrew, Cannon, Davies, Thomas, Murphy, Coughlan, Robertson, Cirino. 
 Only Myles Lewis-Skelly and Viktor Gyokeres keep their place in Arsenal's starting XI from their 2-0 win against Everton on Saturday.
 Illan Meslier makes his debut in goal after joining in the summer, while 18-year-old Northern Ireland international Ceadach O'Neill makes his first senior appearance for the club.
 Mikel Arteta also starts teenagers Max Dowman and Marli Salmon, who both featured in the third-round win over Ipswich. 
 Arsenal XI: Meslier, Timber, Salmon, Mosquera, Hincapie, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman, O'Neill, Havertz, Gyokeres. 
 Subs : Arrizabalaga, White, Odegaard, Eze, Konsa, Guimaraes, Harriman-Annous, Washington, Hashi.

 Hello! published at 19:00 GMT 19:00 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images The last 16.
 This is where clubs start to get serious.
 Win this one and then, well, it's the quarters. You're only two rounds from Wembley.
 Sure the early rounds were for squad rotation, but now it's time to lock in. There are trophies to be won.
